member.name: T:TerraScale.DotNet.TerraScaleSyncV1ViewEngine
member.summary:
The native terrascale.sync.v1 client-side view engine (ADR-0024): one server-authoritative authorized query result, its logical session states, its snapshot assembly, its result revisions, its opaque checkpoint, its acknowledgements, and its reversible optimistic presentation.
The engine implements the published state-machine semantics only. It owns no transport, no MessagePack framing, and no route: the public wire binding lands with the owning public contract and the engine-owned golden corpus, and conformance is claimed only through that corpus. Every mutation is online and server-authoritative; the optimistic layer is presentation that never advances a revision or a checkpoint and never becomes durable state.

member.name: M:TerraScale.DotNet.TerraScaleSyncV1ViewEngine.ApplyResultDelta(TerraScale.DotNet.TerraScaleViewResultDelta)
member.summary: Applies one ResultDelta under the ADR-0024 rules: a delta whose to_revision is already applied is an ignored duplicate; a from_revision that does not match the applied revision is a gap that applies nothing and requires resume or reset; otherwise the operations apply atomically — removals run before the inserts that may reuse a visible key, identity selects the row, a move may accompany an update, and a Reset replaces the complete result. A delta that assumes client state the engine cannot prove (unknown identity, moved-from position mismatch) diverges the view: nothing applies, the generation closes, and an authorized snapshot is required.
member.returns: The typed delivery: applied, reset, duplicate, gap, or divergence.

member.name: M:TerraScale.DotNet.TerraScaleSyncV1ViewEngine.NotifyAuthorizationChange(System.UInt64,TerraScale.DotNet.TerraScaleViewAuthorizationEffect)
member.summary: Records an authorization generation change. A non-revoked change expects the next delivery to open a new view generation: the server emits removals or a bounded diff or a fresh snapshot — the engine accepts whichever arrives first and never resumes the old generation as if its permissions were current. A revoked session drops its checkpoint and closes: no new view work applies.
member.param: The change's effect on this view.
